question:
(i) Explain why total internal reflection can occur only when light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium.
(ii) Use the wavefront idea to explain what happens as the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.

options.A:
(i) Total internal reflection occurs only from denser to rarer medium when $i>c$, because the refracted ray bends away from the normal and at $i=c$ grazes the boundary.
(ii) By Huygens construction, at the critical angle the refracted wavefront lies along the boundary. For $i>c$, a refracted wavefront cannot be constructed in the rarer medium, so light is completely reflected back.
options.B:
(i) Total internal reflection occurs only from rarer to denser medium.
(ii) Above critical angle, refraction becomes stronger into the rarer medium.
options.C:
(i) TIR occurs at every angle when light enters a denser medium.
(ii) At critical angle, light stops propagating.
options.D:
(i) TIR is due to diffraction at the boundary.
(ii) For angles greater than critical angle, the ray passes normally into the rarer medium.
